outputs.rationale: Out of order streaming is a declarative HTML mechanism with no programmatic return value; patched content renders in place rather than producing a value a script reads.

errors.rationale: The mechanism throws no programmatic exceptions, and the page documents no failure mode such as an unmatched template for target; markers are inert annotation nodes.

context.rationale: The feature has no scriptable context object; it operates at the HTML parser/streaming level, and the page's motivational background section carries no addressable id.

lifecycle.rationale: Declarative streaming markup has no programmable instantiation or teardown lifecycle; markers and templates are parsed once during document streaming.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The mechanism exposes no new sensitive information, device capability, or permission surface; it is a document-parsing behavior that reorders streamed content.

notes: Added ids to headings: syntax (h3 '1. Marker processing instructions — the placeholder'), browser-support (h2 'browser support'), see-also (h2 'see also'). The 'the two primitives' h2 opens immediately with an h3, so per the fragment rule it cannot take the syntax id; syntax therefore anchors the first primitive, whose slice contains both the <?marker> prose and a complete marker+template code example. examples and inputs are anchored to #syntax for that reason, and the dedicated 'end-to-end example (server perspective)' section is unaddressable under the three canonical ids. The template-for and range-marker syntax live in sibling h3s.
